audio_caption: The audio clip starts with a dramatic, suspenseful music piece. Then a man's voice announces, "Preview". This is followed by the same dramatic music continuing. The scene then shifts to a male speaker who describes the search for Nibiru. He explains how people have been searching for it and wonders why they search for it. The speaker sounds calm and informational. He continues to discuss how even though modern times have not discovered the planet, it is impossible for it to not exist. The speaker then announces "going to tell you why".

The clip begins with music that has a mysterious tone. An adult male speaker discusses ancient and modern evidence for the existence of another planet, Nibiru, but states that he won't give "false evidence." He conveys that Nibiru is very far away and has a highly irregular orbit period that could rewrite beliefs about our position in the solar system. His tone turns more excited and he invites the listener to hear evidence. The clip concludes with a brief transition to an ominous sound.

The audio clip starts with a male speaker narrating about irregularities in Neptune and Uranus's orbit. He mentions the "trans-Neptunian region" and Percival Lowells' quest for Planet X, speaking in an informative tone. Then, the speaker describes the Planet X hypothesis and discrepancies in the orbits of the giant planets, particularly Uranus and Neptune. In the background, there is subtle music playing which adds a mysterious and inquisitive mood to the narration.

The audio clip starts with an informative narration delivered by a male speaker who sounds articulate and factual, as he discusses Tombaus's discovery of Pluto and its designation as the ninth planet. He then moves on to Pluto's reevaluation in 1978, noting its insufficient size to influence larger planets, and the subsequent, ultimately abandoned, search for a tenth planet. During the entire speech, there is a background music consisting of ominous, slow, and suspenseful music.

The clip begins with speech; a single male speaker, presenting factual information, perhaps in a narration style, mentions "2014," a "super Earth planet," and "astronomical units." The speaker continues, stating that further work in 2016 showed this distant planet is likely "on an inclined, highly eccentric orbit." He concludes by acknowledging the difficulty of constant observation due to the planet's distance. This is accompanied by background music, in an electronic style, that is moody and atmospheric.

The clip begins with a male speaker posing a question regarding ancient Sumerian texts and depictions, specifically asking how the civilization could have had more advanced astronomical knowledge than modern society. He references the Sumerians' depiction of Nibiru, and mentions beings coming to Earth to mine gold to save Nibiru. The speaker continues, stating the beings are known as the Anunnaki and that they were worshipped as gods on Earth. While acknowledging the difficulty in deciphering Sumerian astronomical texts, he states this has been accomplished, and that depictions of Nibiru are understood. He concludes by suggesting that modern society may be overcomplicating its understanding of the sky, and that the answers to deepest questions may be missed. A brief musical interlude that sounds mysterious, somewhat eerie, and space-like with electronic tones, follows, before ending.

The clip begins with a single male speaker setting up a list and introducing Carlos Munoz Ferrada, a figure linked to Nibiru. The speaker says that Ferrada predicted earthquakes in South America, making correlations between astronomical phenomena and earth events. He also predicted the arrival of a "comet planet Nibiru." The tone is serious and informative.

The clip opens with a calm male voice discussing a "Chilean astronomer" who made predictions about celestial events and accurately forecast an earthquake in 1939, noting his "mathematical accuracy," and emphasizing the near-exact date prediction, being only "wrong by a difference of two hours". The speaker highlights the tragic loss of life caused by this earthquake. The male voice also references earthquakes in "1960 and 1980."

The audio clip begins with an informative male voice discussing a planet called Nibiru, explaining that it will become visible and that world events will intensify as it gets closer, but not to worry. He speculates that humans may have colonized the galaxy by the time events intensify. Sounds of a dramatic sting play in the background.

The clip begins with a male speaker introducing "cataclysms on Earth," referring to world catastrophes throughout history. His tone is informative. He mentions giants, dinosaurs, and 20-foot insects that once roamed the Earth. He continues discussing a cataclysm 12,000 years ago and the Sumerian astronomers who depicted the planet Nibiru, suggesting it might be the cause. He mentions the Anunnaki of Nibiru mining Earth for gold, cautioning that the idea sounds crazy. This is followed by a sustained audio effect that is metallic and echoed.

The audio begins with a male speaker describing "the asteroid belt" as a strange place located between Mars and Jupiter. The speaker has a somewhat serious, almost dramatic tone. He suggests the belt may have been a planet that collided with the Nibiru system. The clip contains background music that fits the overall tone of the speech.

The audio begins with a male speaker discussing the discovery of asteroids orbiting the sun. His tone is informative and conversational. He notes the disagreement among catastrophists regarding a missing planet. Simultaneously, there is an ominous background music that sets an unsettling tone. He references a planet known to the Sumerians as "Tiamat." The music then ceases abruptly.

The audio clip starts with a speaker discussing ancient Sumerian texts, referencing "Tiamat" being struck by a planet, creating "the Earth's moon and the asteroid belt." The speaker then mentions Zechariah Sitchin and the "celestial battle." The tone is informative and somewhat serious. The speaker continues describing the planet "Nibiru" striking Tiamat. A brief, quiet "What?" sound can be heard.

The clip begins with a male speaker, calmly explaining how Nibiru's satellites and then Nibiru itself struck Tiamat, shattering the planet. He mentions the Sumerians calling it "the great band," and the creation of Earth's moon and the asteroid belt. The speaker's tone is informational, like a lecture.  A brief sound effect, possibly a whoosh or explosion, concludes the clip.

The audio clip begins with an upbeat, lighthearted electronic music track, creating a sense of anticipation. Then, a male speaker with a measured tone begins, focusing on Planet Nine as "number one on our list," highlighting the observation of a "speck of light." The speaker continues describing the discovery and the anticipation surrounding it, stressing the importance of confirming the existence of the planet, and the potential for discovering it in the near future. The electronic music resumes at the end, maintaining its cheerful, optimistic tone.

The clip begins with a male speaker, in a neutral tone, describing a hypothetical "Planet Nine". According to the speaker, this object would have a mass "about 10 times that of Earth" and orbit "about 20 times farther than the sun on an average of Neptune", taking 20,000 years to complete a full orbit. He further explains that "some of the dwarf planets and other small, icy objects tend to follow orbits that cluster together."

The audio clip begins with a male speaker talking about analyzing orbits and the possibility of a "large, previously undiscovered planet" beyond Pluto. He speaks in a factual, informative tone. He continues, estimating that the planet's gravity "may explain the unusual orbits" of Kuiper Belt objects. A question wraps up the speech portion: "what do you think of our selections here?" No music or background sounds are present in this clip.

The audio clip begins with speech from a male speaker who is confident and earnest. He hopes the listener enjoyed the "evidence" presented and accuses people of spreading "false information surrounding this planet" that discredits people "dedicating their lives in the search for the planet Nibiru." This is followed by a suspenseful, ominous track, suggestive of science fiction or thriller. The track's tension is further built with a low-frequency drone sound.
